hostedFailure.test: successful and terminated parents cannot leave their owned process group running

error.stack: async readFileHandle → exited at recipe.test.mjs:50 → descendant observation at :80

diagnosis.rootCause: Linux procfs distinguishes absence before open (ENOENT/open) from a task disappearing after its proc file was opened but before its read is fulfilled (ESRCH/read). The observation predicate only recognized ENOENT, so successful cleanup/reaping could surface as a test error.

new-open.message: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/proc/136730/stat'
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/proc/136735/stat'
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/proc/136736/stat'
ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/proc/136737/stat'

diagnosis.determinism: Four predeclared native samples: hold an unread /proc/owned-child/stat descriptor while alive, kill only that child, await Node close/reap, then perform a fresh path open and the held-descriptor read. Every sample returned ENOENT/open and ESRCH/read respectively. No timing retry, load, fake error code or deadline change was needed.

repair: Accept only ENOENT or ESRCH as an absent process in the test-local proc observation predicate. Keep live state classification unchanged and rethrow other read failures.
Keep the same 40 × 25 ms bounded native observation, 150 ms readiness-triggered timeout clock, wall-clock timeout/log/cancel tests, fixed runner errors and owned group cleanup.

Within the existing descendant case, assert an actual live native child is not exited; open proc while alive, kill/reap the owned child, feed the actual held descriptor read through the predicate, and assert actual ESRCH/read. EACCES and EIO are required to propagate unchanged.
The test-local optional reader only controls the native open/read boundary for this regression; no production runner/helper/module was introduced.

verification.result: 4/4 deterministic native ENOENT/open versus ESRCH/read observations; all owned direct children killed and reaped.
